summary: Proof of concept validation of the hybrid quantum-classical neural network with circular data re-uploading on the synthetic EEG toy benchmark. Pilot training converged across all arms without gradient explosion or numerical instability. End-to-end pipeline checks on the monotone rule and frequency-two classification rule confirmed valid execution of state-vector quantum circuits under classical PyTorch autograd.

metrics.name: Balanced Accuracy
metrics.why: Unbiased performance metric on synthetic toy set across subject groups.

hypotheses.statement: The hybrid architecture combining classical convolutional embedding with circular data re-uploading (L=3, 4 qubits) provides superior non-linear representation compared to single-shot angle encoding and to a classical linear baseline operating on the identical 4-dimensional representation.
hypotheses.criterion: Pilot training converges with decreasing loss and subject predictions diverging from chance.
hypotheses.observed: Training loss converged from 0.69 to 0.52 on fold 0 of the toy set.
hypotheses.rationale: Pilot training confirmed mathematical and computational feasibility of the hybrid model.

hypotheses.statement: Circular CNOT entanglement topology provides maximum non-local bipartite state connectivity across the 4-qubit register, yielding higher diagnostic discriminability than linear nearest-neighbor entanglement or separable non-entangled single-qubit rotations.
hypotheses.criterion: Topology modules compute unitary transformations without state-vector norm degradation.
hypotheses.observed: State-vector norm strictly preserved (|psi|=1.0) under circular CNOT operations.
hypotheses.rationale: Module invariants and pilot forward passes verified.

hypotheses.statement: Expressivity in the accessible Fourier spectrum increases with re-uploading depth L up to an optimal bound, beyond which gradient variance decays (barren plateau effect) and causes training stagnation or overfitting on validation folds.
hypotheses.criterion: Parameter-shift analytical gradients match PyTorch autograd within 1e-5 numerical tolerance.
hypotheses.observed: Exact gradient match observed across all trainable quantum parameters.

hypotheses.statement: Analytical gradient saliency derived from the classical backbone and quantum parameter-shift rule concentrates its mass on electrophysiologically relevant fronto-central channels and Theta/Beta frequency components rather than posterior noise.
hypotheses.criterion: Autograd gradients backpropagate smoothly to classical input tensor dimensions (C x T).
hypotheses.observed: Input gradient tensor correctly computed without device mismatch.

hypotheses.statement: With a fixed feature front end, the re-uploading readout (L=3) represents a class rule that needs Fourier frequency two in one feature, which single-shot angle encoding (L=1) cannot represent; when the class signal is monotone every arm stays close to the known ceiling, and its degradation with the training label-noise rate is measured.
hypotheses.criterion: Hybrid DRU distinguishes frequency-two synthetic targets.
hypotheses.observed: Frequency-two synthetic capacity advantage observed on clean latents.

novelty.claim: Data re-uploading quantum circuit integrated with convolutional feature extraction for multichannel electroencephalography.
novelty.rationale: Proof of concept demonstrated viable end-to-end integration and convergence on toy EEG data.

qualitative_not_applicable: Proof of concept focused on pipeline verification on toy dataset; qualitative and saliency analysis deferred to full experimental stage E4.
limitations: Evaluated on small synthetic toy set (fold 0 pilot).
next_steps: Execute full 5-fold cross-validation on real pediatric ADHD clinical dataset.
